slides.sub: The biggest lie you've been told about mortgage shopping: every lender check hurts your score again.

slides.label: The myth:
slides.title: Every lender check hurts you again
slides.body: So you only talk to one lender and never compare offers.
slides.source: CFPB, What happens when a mortgage lender checks my credit? (Oct. 2026)

slides.label: The fact:
slides.title: Checks within 45 days count as one
slides.body: Multiple mortgage credit checks show up as a single inquiry, as long as the last one is within 45 days of the first.
slides.source: CFPB, What happens when a mortgage lender checks my credit? (Oct. 2026)

slides.label: Your shopping window
slides.body: Line up your lender quotes inside it. The CFPB says an inquiry typically has a small negative effect on your scores.
slides.source: CFPB, What happens when a mortgage lender checks my credit? (Oct. 2026)

slides.label: One more:
slides.title: Hold off on other new credit until you close
slides.body: Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
slides.source: CFPB, What happens when a mortgage lender checks my credit? (Oct. 2026)

caption:
The biggest lie you've been told about mortgage shopping: every lender check hurts your score again.

Here's what the CFPB says. Multiple credit checks from mortgage lenders show up on your credit report as a single inquiry, as long as the last one is within 45 days of the first. An inquiry typically has a small negative effect on your scores. So line up your lender quotes inside that window, and hold off on applying for other credit right before or during the mortgage process.

Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
